title: He didn’t need money.
paragraphs: And that’s the part we miss.
Because if we’re honest… we’re still sitting at the gate.
Still managing what God wants to transform.
The man in Acts 3 wasn’t dreaming of walking.
That dream died a long time ago.
Years of disappointment have a way of shrinking your faith.
You stopped believing God could change that part of your life.
That quiet shame nobody knows about.
You don’t even ask for freedom anymore.
Just enough to get through today.
Sitting at the gate called Beautiful.
You can look close to God…
And still be stuck in sin.
And still carry chains no one sees.
But with something far more dangerous.
“Silver and gold have I none; but such as I have give I thee: In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth rise up and walk.” (Acts 3:6)
And here’s the part that confronts us:
The man didn’t even ask for healing.
Because God will not always answer the prayer you pray…
He will answer the need you’re too broken to see.
Some of us don’t need more blessings.
Some of us don’t need open doors.
Some of us don’t need comfort.
Because sin doesn’t just wound you.
It teaches you how to live below your calling.
It convinces you that bondage is normal.
That this is just who you are.
“Immediately his feet and ankle bones received strength.” (Acts 3:7)
That’s what happens when Jesus steps in.
He said, “In the name of Jesus…”
Because the power was never in the man.
And it’s not in you either.
Unable to stand before a holy God on our own.
“For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.” (Romans 3:23)
And God didn’t throw us coins from heaven.
Jesus Christ lived the life we could not live.
Then He went to the cross.
“But God shows his love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” (Romans 5:8)
He took the weight of our shame.
Through repentance and faith in Him—
“If anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation.” (2 Corinthians 5:17)
When Jesus is calling you to stand?
When grace is offering you a new life?
When the cross already exposed and covered your sin?
And hear this, not as a quote—
But as a call over your life:
“In the name of Jesus Christ… rise up and walk.”
If this hit something deep in you…
